title: SRE handoff and SLO health snapshot — week of May 18-24, 2026
content:
Goal: quick operational snapshot for the SRE rotation and FYI for platform teams. Use this as the single handoff doc for the week; runbook edits are below.

Summary (one line):
- Two brief degradations this week (one cache eviction-related API latency blip, one regional autoscaler misfire); both resolved with fallbacks and post-incident mitigations queued. No customer-facing data loss.

Incidents and status:
1) INCIDENT INF-2398 — cache-driver-induced tokenization latency spike (May 19 local peak)
   - Impact: 5xx rate rose from 0.1% to 1.8% for 18 minutes for hosted.text.generate in us-west-2; median latency increased 2.1x.
   - Root cause (current hypothesis): a rare cache-eviction race in the prefix cache causing synchronous serialization on the request path under a burst from a single customer test harness.
   - Mitigation performed: roll forward partial KV cache guard (hotfix deployed by on-call Jordan Li at 09:34 PDT), temporary rate-limit backpressure applied to offending API key at 09:41 PDT.
   - Post-mortem notes: urgent runbook item to add eviction circuit-breaker; ticket created INF-2410 to add metrics and a canary test. Owner: Priya Menon.

2) INCIDENT INF-2410 — autoscaler scaling jitter in eu-central-1 (May 22 early morning)
   - Impact: brief capacity oscillation causing queued requests and tail latency spikes for dedicated customers on the EU pool.
   - Root cause: combination of aggressive pod termination grace settings and a mis-evaluated CPU-based scaling threshold during a garbage-collection-heavy deployment.
   - Mitigation: temporary widening of autoscale thresholds and deploy rollback; SLO guardrails enforced via routing to secondary pool.
   - Follow-ups: change autoscaler policy to include memory/GPU-utilization signals and add a 60s stabilization window. Owner: Mateo Alvarez.

SLO / Metric snapshot (rolling 7d as of 2026-05-26):
- hosted.text.generate availability (99.95 target): 99.973% (green)
- p50 latency (text.generate): 120ms (target < 150ms)
- p95 latency (text.generate): 670ms (target < 600ms) — slight regression driven by eu-central-1 autoscale jitter above
- error rate (4xx+5xx) overall: 0.28% (target < 0.5%)
- KV cache hit rate (serving-runtime): 87% (target > 90%) — note drop correlates with INF-2398

Operational actions this week (ordered):
- High priority: add eviction circuit-breaker and make KV cache eviction asynchronous (INF-2410). Owner: Priya. ETA: 2026-06-04.
- Medium: extend autoscaler stabilization window and add GPU/mem signal (infra PR #402). Owner: Mateo. ETA: 2026-06-01.
- Low: add synthetic canary traffic that exercises prefix-cache eviction patterns; schedule weekly run for next 2 months. Owner: Jordan. ETA: 2026-06-10.
- Dashboard: add a dedicated panel for 'cache-eviction-rate' and per-key hot-spot heatmap. Owner: Aisha. ETA: 2026-05-31.

On-call handoff notes (for next rotation):
- Current on-call: Jordan Li (primary), Priya Menon (secondary) — rotation ends 2026-05-28 08:00 PDT. Next on-call primary: Mateo Alvarez.
- Hot keys and throttles: If you see sustained 5xx > 0.8% for more than 10 minutes, escalate to Priya and toggle per-key backpressure for heavy-emitters (see runbook section 'per-key throttles').
- Escalation matrix: primary -> secondary -> SRE lead (Aisha) -> Eng infra pager. Pager channel: #sre-oncall; log all step actions to the incident JIRA.

Runbook edits and quick links (edits made 2026-05-26):
- Added 'eviction-circuit-breaker' step with exact curl commands for the guard feature (see linked_artifacts).
- Clarified autoscaler dev deployment checklist to include a staged GC test.
- New runbook snippet: how to safely reroute traffic to backup dedicated pools without dropping client conferences (copy below).

Capacity and upcoming risks:
- Capacity: Dedicated EU pool currently at 72% committed GPU during peak; projected to hit 80% by mid-June with customer X ramp. Recommend booking burst window or enabling additional reserved capacity routing for 2 hours during night ramp testing.
- Risk: increased model sizes from product team could increase KV cache pressure; cross-team sync scheduled with model-onboarding on 2026-05-29.

Action items for product/infra/product-ops:
- Product: Provide expected model rollout schedule for June-July by 2026-05-28.
- Infra: Prioritize infra PR #402 (autoscaler) and run Perf CI gate for GC-heavy deploys.
- CS: Notify Dedicated customers of potential maintenance window if autoscaler stabilization requires short routing changes (TBD).

Notes / Loose threads:
- Need to confirm whether the customer test harness in INF-2398 violated our acceptable-use throttles; reaching out to account team.
- Decide whether to treat KV cache hit rate as an explicit SLO (proposal in Confluence).

Attachments / refs:
- JIRA INF-2398 (incident), INF-2410 (follow-ups)
- GitHub PR: infra#402 (autoscaler policy)
- Slack threads: #sre-oncall (link pinned), #infra-deploys (GC discussion)

Handoff checklist (next on-call take these first 30 minutes):
- Read this doc and check SLO dashboard (link in linked_artifacts).
- Confirm primary region health (us-west-2, eu-central-1 panels).
- Run the 'cache-eviction canary' (script path: /infra/tools/cache-canary.sh) and report results as comment on INF-2398.
- Ensure runbook 'per-key throttles' steps are reachable and that feature toggle service is healthy.

Final notes:
- Overall system remains within SLO bounds; incidents exposed brittle corners in cache eviction and autoscaling logic. Priorities for the next two weeks: fix eviction async path, harden autoscaler signals, and add canaries.

Prepared by: Aisha Patel (SRE lead)
Reviewed: Jordan Li, Priya Menon
